html:
A renewed, escalating conflict between the United States and Iran over the Strait of Hormuz dominates global affairs, with US strikes targeting Iran and Tehran retaliating against Gulf states and oil tankers, prompting Trump to announce a naval blockade and transit toll for the critical waterway.

US-Iran Conflict: The United States has launched a third night of strikes on Iran, reportedly hitting between 140 and 170 Iranian targets across the Islamic Republic in 48 hours, after Iran hit two oil tankers in the Strait of Hormuz, killing a crew member. Iran has claimed retaliatory strikes on US airbases in Jordan and Bahrain, as well as targets in Kuwait and Qatar, with photos circulating of damage to the Al Udeid base. Trump has declared the US will reinstate a blockade over the Strait of Hormuz, vowing to become "guardians of the Strait of Hormuz" and charge a 20% cargo fee for transit, a move denounced as "piracy" by Brazil's Lula. Iran's military spokesperson affirmed that its armed forces will not back down on Iran's rights in the Strait. Germany, France, and the UK have condemned Iran’s attacks, while China urges both nations to restore safe passage, as the conflict raises oil prices to their highest point since last month's peace deal.

Russia-Ukraine: Ukraine has targeted another 11 Russian ships in the Sea of Azov and launched drone assaults on Russian oil facilities, including the Afipsky Refinery. These attacks have led to a deepening fuel crisis in Russia, with gasoline output covering only 65% of demand and state contracts for essential services like hospitals collapsing. Meanwhile, in Ukraine, parliament accepted PM Svyrydenko's resignation as Volodymyr Zelenskyy moves to reshuffle the cabinet, signaling a shift in the country's "political strategy."

European Security: France hosted its largest-ever Bastille Day military parade, showcasing European unity for Ukraine, with President Emmanuel Macron reviewing troops including 500 from a "coalition of the willing." The event underscored Europe's rearmament and strategic autonomy, with French Rafale fighter jets actively patrolling Lithuanian airspace to deter Russian drones and planes. Separately, the EU moved to ban gold imports from Sudan and restrict exports of mining chemicals to curb war financing.

Global Economy & Markets: The escalating tensions in the Strait of Hormuz have driven oil prices to a four-week high, raising concerns among economists that renewed conflict with Iran could necessitate a fourth interest rate rise in Australia this year. In a sign of shifting global demand, diamond giant De Beers announced it would halt production for two years at a flagship South African mine, impacting over 4,000 employees. Furthermore, a global survey suggests that productivity is dropping worldwide due to the World Cup.

MENA Regional Conflicts & Security: Beyond the US-Iran confrontation, Israeli strikes on a police post in north Gaza killed seven, including a senior officer, and resulted in a Palestinian child killed and dozens injured in southern Gaza, with further strikes injuring Palestinians in central Gaza. Lebanon and Israel held US-brokered talks in Rome regarding a framework deal, with Israel expressing readiness to advance a pullback from two "pilot areas." In Yemen, Houthis launched missiles at Saudi Arabia's Abha airport in response to Saudi strikes on Sanaa airport.

Domestic Policy & Social Issues: New York became the first US state to impose a one-year moratorium on new AI datacenters through an executive order by Governor Kathy Hochul, citing concerns over their resource intensity. In the UK, the latest Covid inquiry report found the Johnson government wasted £10bn on PPE, a conclusion welcomed by campaigners despite skepticism over the verdict on a 'VIP lane'. In the US, separate incidents in Houston and Maine saw ICE agents fatally shoot an undocumented migrant and a Colombian national, respectively, triggering anti-ICE demonstrations.
